comparison: Both strongly support the novel methodological approach using radiomics and dimensionality reduction on histological data (C3, C4, C34, C37, C38, C87, C89, C90). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of parameters and spatial patterns, while peer reviewers emphasize the novelty and power of the data-driven parcellation approach. Complete agreement on methodological contribution.

Perfect alignment on translation to in vivo data (C7, C65-C72). Both acknowledge the successful translation of histological findings to 7T MRI with consistent U1 findings across subjects. OpenEval notes the small sample size (n=10) as a limitation, while peer reviewers affirm the combination of histology with in vivo imaging as a strength. Both accept the lower consistency of U2.

Perfect agreement on acknowledged limitations (C97, C98, C109, C118-C121). Both recognize the small sample size, U2 inconsistency, spatial autocorrelation effects, and technical challenges. OpenEval provides detailed enumeration of limitations, while peer reviewers acknowledge these do not undermine core contributions. Both view limitations as appropriately contextualized.

Both support the spatial correlation findings and validation against expert labels. OpenEval focuses on quantitative validation of U1's inferior-superior gradient (C5, C53-C57), while peer reviewers emphasize the broader finding of microstructural axes and their validation (C5, C6, C53-C57, C59-C63). Strong agreement on core histological findings.

Both support validation against expert-labeled data. OpenEval emphasizes the strong statistical validation (C6, C58-C63, F=1630.8) demonstrating biological validity, while peer reviewers affirm the identification of structural clusters and microstructural axes more broadly (C5, C6, C59-C63). Agreement on validation strength.

Strong agreement on functional connectivity findings (C8, C73-C77). OpenEval provides detailed methodological validation of the connectivity analysis with appropriate statistical controls, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the distinct connectivity patterns to cortical networks. Both support the structure-function relationship.

Both support meta-analytic decoding findings (C78-C80). OpenEval notes the method is sound but cautions about reverse inference limitations, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the associations with autobiographical memory and emotional face processing. OpenEval is more cautious about interpretation specificity.

Strong agreement on framework advantages and applicability (C84, C93-C96, C99, C129-C132). OpenEval articulates specific methodological improvements while noting need for broader validation, while peer reviewers emphasize the individual-level applicability and holistic micro-to-macro approach. Both view this as a valuable methodological contribution.

Both address broader implications and future applications (C85, C86, C133, C134). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN/SPECULATION since clinical utility is not demonstrated in current work, while peer reviewers support the potential for advancing research. Difference in emphasis: OpenEval distinguishes aspirational goals from established results, peer reviewers affirm the promise.

Overlap on contribution to broader research program (C131, C132). OpenEval views transformative clinical impact as undemonstrated speculation, while peer reviewers emphasize the impressive holistic approach and individual-level applicability as current contributions. Different framing of present vs. future impact.

Minimal overlap on UMAP application (C47). OpenEval provides detailed validation of UMAP methodology and interpretation of U1/U2 dimensions, while peer reviewers mention the broader finding of microstructural axes without specifically discussing UMAP. OpenEval provides more technical depth on dimensionality reduction.

Limited overlap on right hemisphere replication (C64). OpenEval specifically validates bilateral consistency as strengthening the findings, while peer reviewers include this in their general affirmation of microstructural organization findings. Both support the finding but with different emphasis.

Minimal overlap on framework utility (C81). OpenEval discusses complementary nature to prior approaches and framework advantages, while peer reviewers focus on functional connectivity findings. Both ultimately support the contribution but address different aspects.

OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of contextualization with prior literature (C110-C112, C117, C124, C127-C128), including convergence with other methodologies and connections to chemoarchitecture. Notes some claims are speculative. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers generally affirm the findings.

OpenEval evaluates anatomical correspondence and functional associations (C114-C116, C126), noting quantitative validation supports anatomical claims but fear-related associations are more speculative. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation, though these findings are implicitly included in peer reviewers' general support.

OpenEval provides detailed methodological evaluation of data sources and preprocessing (C135-C146), validating the conservative approach and acknowledging single-subject histology limitation. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation of these methodological details.

OpenEval thoroughly evaluates MRI acquisition and processing pipeline (C152-C160), affirming appropriate methods and noting small sample size. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation of these technical details, though peer reviewers affirm the overall in vivo translation.
